problem:
Consider the following set of functions:

$$
{f}_{1}(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,{f}_{2}(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,{f}_{3}(t)=t
$$

Given that the inner product in the vector space $C[0,\pi ]$ of continuous functions over $[0,\pi ]$ is defined as 

$$
⟨f(t),g(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(t)g(t)\,\text{d}t,
$$

which of the following statements are true?

- ${f}_{1}(t)⊥{f}_{2}(t)$ with respect to the given inner product
- ${f}_{1}(t)⊥{f}_{3}(t)$ with respect to the given inner product
- $S={{f}_{1}(t),{f}_{2}(t),{f}_{3}(t)}$ is an orthogonal set with respect to the given inner product

choices.value: None of the statements are true

activity_context.topic_title: Orthogonal Sets in Inner Product Spaces
